title: EU data localization and customer KMS playbook
body:
Summary:
This doc captures the workshop outcome with ACME Health (simulated customer) on EU-only data residency, per-customer KMS/HSM separation, and short-term telemetry retention for POCs. Goal: produce a concrete implementation playbook and a short DPA addendum draft that the legal and sales teams can iterate on.

Context / ask from customer:
- Customer requires all customer-provided prompts and model responses for their POC to remain in EU data centers (region: eu-west1) and never egress to US-based logs or analytics.
- They want the ability to provide their own KMS keys (BYOK) for encrypting request payloads at rest.
- Telemetry/metrics must be sampled and scrubbed before leaving the region; raw request content must be retained no longer than 7 days by default and optionally set to 0 days (ephemeral) during sensitive tests.
- Audit logs and administrative traces should be exportable to the customer's GCS bucket locked by a signed IAM role.

Constraints identified in workshop:
- Hosted API currently aggregates some usage telemetry in a global telemetry pipeline (centralized ingestion). Need to provide regionally isolated ingestion path or guarantee in-flight and at-rest separation for EU customers.
- Some inference fallback paths (model variants in other regions) exist; fallback behavior must remain within EU or be disabled for these customers.
- BYOK integration is supported but needs per-tenant key rotation guidance and clear operator runbooks.

Recommended solution (high level):
1) Regional deployment model: Dedicated EU tenant in eu-west1 (Dedicated or Private mode) with VPC endpoints and regional-only routing.
   - All inference nodes, KV caches, logs, and prefix caches provisioned in eu-west1.
   - Smart routing policy: for customer tag "eu-only" block cross-region fallbacks.

2) Customer-managed KMS/HSM (BYOK):
   - Support two modes:
     a) Pass-through envelope encryption: Redwood stores only ciphertext; customer KMS holds DEK (data encryption key) wrapped by KEK in customer's KMS.
     b) HSM attestation option for enterprise customers (onboarding via security team).
   - Key rotation: outline script + recommended rotation cadence (90 days default for DEK wrapping rotation).

3) Retention and telemetry policy enforcement:
   - Retention tiers: ephemeral (0 days), short_term (7 days), audit (90 days for non-content telemetry only).
   - Default for EU POC: short_term (7 days) for content logs, telemetry aggregated and anonymized in-region, exportable to customer's bucket within 24h.
   - Implement server-side policy enforcement point that drops content after TTL expires and emits an audit event (non-content) to a separate audit store.

4) Network & egress controls:
   - VPC Service Controls or customer-managed firewall rules to restrict egress to eu-west1 endpoints only.
   - Disable third-party integrations that route logs outside EU (analytics, alerting endpoints) for the tenant.

5) Auditability and proofs:
   - Provide a signed snapshot (signed by Redwood HSM) showing that retention job ran and deleted content at TTL.
   - Provide access to system-generated audit logs (admin operations) to customer's GCS bucket.

Sample data flow (text):
- Customer -> HTTPS -> Regional API gateway (eu-west1) -> Tenant inference pool -> KMS encrypt/decrypt via customer key wrapper -> Temporary prefix/KV cache (in-region) -> Response returned to customer.
- Request content stored in content-store with retention metadata. After TTL, deletion job runs and pushes deletion-signed receipt to audit-store.

Minimal retention policy pseudo-SLA (to include in DPA addendum):
- "Customer Content" means prompt text, files, attachments, and model responses submitted by Customer or end-users.
- Storage: Customer Content will be stored in eu-west1. Redwood will retain Customer Content in readable form for a maximum of 7 days by default, unless Customer specifies 'ephemeral' (0 days) in writing.
- Deletion: At the end of the retention period Redwood will permanently delete Customer Content from primary content stores and trigger deletion from backups within 30 days. Redwood will provide a signed deletion receipt within 48 hours of deletion.

Sample DPA addendum clause (draft language for legal):
"Processing Location and Retention. Vendor shall process and store Customer Data exclusively within the European Union (eu-west1) for the duration of the Services. Vendor shall, upon Customer's selection of the 'ephemeral' retention profile, delete Customer Content immediately after request completion and shall provide an auditable deletion receipt. For the 'short_term' profile, Vendor shall delete Customer Content within seven (7) days of ingestion. Vendor will ensure any backups containing Customer Content are scheduled for deletion or irrecoverable redaction no later than thirty (30) days following primary-store deletion. Vendor will offer Customer the option to supply and manage encryption keys via Customer's KMS; in such case Vendor will only store wrapped keys and will not have access to the unwrapped key material."

Operational checklist for POC (implementation runbook):
- [ ] Create eu-west1 tenant, attach project id (owner: Ravi Patel, due: 2026-03-12)
- [ ] Enable region-only routing and disable cross-region fallbacks for tenant (owner: Lena Park, due: 2026-03-15)
- [ ] BYOK onboarding: provide key wrapping guide and integration test harness (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2026-03-20)
- [ ] Implement retention-policy enforcement job and signed deletion receipts (owner: Maya Chen, due: 2026-03-22)
- [ ] Configure telemetry aggregation in-region and confirm export path to customer GCS (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-18)
- [ ] Prepare DPA addendum draft and run with legal (owner: Maya Chen, due: 2026-03-10 -> IN PROGRESS)

Notes / gotchas from the workshop:
- Some internal admin tooling currently reads logs from a global index to surface support traces; we must whitelist-only the eu tenant indices to prevent accidental export.
- Backup retention policy for underlying block storage needs to be audited; backup copies may be outside eu-west1 if not configured — ops must confirm region locking.
- Low-latency replication between AZs in the EU region is acceptable, but cross-region replication is not.

Open questions for legal / security teams:
1) Is the 30-day maximum for backup deletion acceptable/legal-complete for regulated health data? (Action: legal to confirm. Owner: Maya Chen)
2) Are signed deletion receipts sufficient as proof for compliance auditors, or do we need notarized/third-party attestations? (Action: security/legal)
3) For BYOK mode, do we require a formal attestation that Redwood cannot decrypt wrapped keys (suggest adding HSM attestation steps)?

Next steps:
- Ship a short 'eu-poc' template (config + runbook) to the solutions-engineering repo that can be cloned per-customer. (Owner: Ravi Patel, ETA: 2026-03-17)
- Legal to iterate on the DPA draft above and return comments. (Owner: Legal: Samir Khan)
- Plan a follow-up workshop with ACME Health to walk through BYOK onboarding and test ephemeral mode. (Owner: Maya Chen, Target week: 2026-03-22)

References and artifacts:
- Confluence: /eu-data-localization (linked above)
- Jira: ENG-4921 (regional routing work)
- SDK snippet for retention flag: POST /v1/generate { "text": "...", "retention_profile": "ephemeral" }

Appendix: Example SDK request (python):
import requests
headers = { 'Authorization': 'Bearer <TOKEN>', 'X-Region-Override': 'eu-west1' }
payload = { 'text': 'Patient note example: ...', 'retention_profile': 'short_term' }
r = requests.post('https://api.eu.redwood.ai/v1/generate', json=payload, headers=headers)

-- end of notes --
